**Grading note (sub-item 1a — 1 point deducted if the possible NPE is not discussed):**

Award no deduction if the answer raises the possibility of a NullPointerException anywhere in its treatment of this code, in any framing. Hypothetical or conditional phrasing is enough — "if mPrefix were null, this would throw an NPE" or "a null mPrefix would NPE here" satisfies the item even when the answer never commits to mPrefix actually being nullable. The NPE also need not be pinpointed to the mPrefix access itself; a possible NPE discussed anywhere in the analysis of this code counts. It likewise counts when the NPE surfaces only in remediation advice or a code comment, e.g. "add a null check to avoid a NullPointerException." Any surfacing of the NPE risk is sufficient.

Deduct 1 point only when the answer never raises the possibility of an NPE at all. This includes answers that affirmatively deny it — claiming no NPE can occur, or that some other exception type is thrown instead — since such answers also failed to convey that an NPE may occur; in those cases this 1-point deduction applies on top of any other deduction taken elsewhere in the rubric (it is not superseded by the 2-point item).

CONFLICT: [1a_mention_in_fix_only] / [1a_hypothetical_framing] / [1a_scope_tied_to_mprefix] vs [1a_applied_to_call_site] — the latter is about a different subject (generic immutable-one-entry-map vs mutable-copy comparison not related to messageParams/the command) and would force a deduction on an answer that nonetheless surfaces the NPE risk somewhere, which the other three forks require to be scored no_deduct.

**Sub-item 2d — "If the answer incorrectly states that mPrefix can be null through some other means, 2 points should be deducted."**

Deduct only when the answer asserts, as a fact or as an actual cause operating in this code, a mechanism for mPrefix being null that is *false given the code* and does not trace back to the value of the cloud-service system property — for example, "mPrefix is null because the constructor never assigns it" or "a method explicitly sets mPrefix = null." Deduct 2 points for each distinct incorrect mechanism asserted this way, subject to the parent item's point cap, so an answer that asserts two such wrong mechanisms loses 4.

Do not deduct when the mechanism the answer gives is merely a restatement or downstream description of the same root cause — e.g., "the switch/if-chain has no matching branch so the field is never assigned," or "the property is unset or empty so no prefix is chosen" — since these still trace back to the cloud-service system property value and are only different wording for the correct cause. Likewise do not deduct for mechanisms that are technically accurate statements about Java or about this class, such as the default null value of a field before assignment, reflection, or thread-visibility effects; this sub-item targets factually incorrect claims, not merely unintended-but-true ones. Finally, do not deduct for alternatives that are hedged, hypothetical, or explicitly flagged as unlikely — framed as speculation rather than as a claim about what happens in this code; only assertive claims count as "states."
